### `c60259fa6acc` — perf(inkling2/cuda): a GGUF's Q8_0 dense matrices stay Q8_0 and run on the int8 tensor cores, one exact GEMM for every batch size

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_cuda.cuh` (+2/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_cuda_backend.cu` (+17/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_kernels.cuh` (+100/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_moe_cuda.cuh` (+16/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_runner.cuh` (+98/-12)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/ink_backend.h` (+2/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/ink_gguf_loader.h` (+62/-7)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/ink_main.cpp` (+20/-4)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/ink_q8f_pack.h` (+44/-0)
  - `engine/tests/cuda/ink_q8f_gemm_test.cu` (+123/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
The Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL file stores the attention matrices (q, k, v, gate, output, rel) and the embedding as Q8_0 (int8 plus an fp16 scale per
32 weights). The loader expanded all of them to BF16: 2 bytes per weight, rounded (int8 x fp16 scale does not fit BF16), about twice the bytes
read per step, and weights that were not the file's.

- Loader (CUDA, one GPU with compute capability 8.0 or newer, no layer split; STRATA_INK_Q8_0_DENSE=0 goes back to BF16): the attention matrices
  become format 105, packed on the host (ink_q8f_pack.h) in the order the int8 mma reads: per 16-row tile and 32-wide block one 16-byte A
  fragment per lane, then the block scales. The embedding becomes format 104 (as stored, row by row) and its kernel decodes a row exactly.
  The unembedding and the sink projection stay BF16; other backends and the CPU backend never set the switch.
- One GEMM (k_ink_gemm_q8f) for decode (1..64 slots) and prefill chunks: the activations are quantized per token and 32-wide block like Q8_1
  (k_ink_quant_x_q8f), every output is the sum over the K/32 blocks, in block order, of the exact int32 block dot times (weight scale x
  activation scale) in fp32 FMA. Nothing depends on M or on the other tokens, so a token gets the same bits whether it is read in a prefill chunk,
  decoded alone or decoded in a batch. The q/r/gate/k/v matrices go in one launch with one activation quantization, at any M; short matrices
  (the output projection) split the tokens over more blocks to keep the card busy.
- Diagnostics: STRATA_INK_PROF=1 prints the per-phase decode time every 100 steps (events only, no sync per phase, eager) and the MoE sub-phases
  (router, bin, gate/up, down); INK_DUMP_CHUNK=n makes --dump-ref feed n tokens at a time.

RTX A6000, UD-Q4_K_XL, all resident, same binary, alternating arms, 3 rounds (spread under 1%), fp8 KV, --draft off, CUDA graph decode:
decode 47 / 4,096 / 63,981 token prompts: 76.2 / 71.7 / 52.3 -> 83.7 / 78.2 / 55.8 tok/s (+10% / +9% / +7%).
prefill: 263 / 919 / 816 -> 269 / 892 / 796 tok/s (+2% / -3% / -2%).
Eager step time by number of slots (bench, tok/s): M=1 59.9 -> 64.0, M=8 216 -> 228, M=32 222 -> 225, M=64 314 -> 319.
Load line trunk=: 3.29 GB -> 2.25 GB. The answers change on purpose (the BF16 rounding of the weights is gone); greedy tokens repeat
bit-identically in every round, and the 5-run logits fingerprint gives one hash for prefill and one for single-token decode.
Tests: engine/tests/cuda/ink_q8f_gemm_test.cu is bit-exact against a host emulation of the same arithmetic and gives identical values at
M = 70, 64, 33, 9, 8, 7, 1 (compute-sanitizer memcheck 0 errors, racecheck 0 hazards); the engine under compute-sanitizer memcheck: 0 errors.
Against strata-ik2 as the oracle on UnbiasedStrata's ledger / museum cases the mean KL stays about 0.01 in prefill, decode and 7-token chunks,
as with BF16 (the oracle is llama.cpp-style arithmetic, not an fp32 reference).
```

### `5ef71af9b28f` — perf(inkling2/sycl): spread the one-token loop-controller, attention-residual mix, router and small F32 kernels over the GPU, bit for bit the same results

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `.github/ci/inkspeed/b70_speed.sh` (+12/-16)
  - `engine/CMakeLists.txt` (+0/-4)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/sycl/ink_sy_codecs.h` (+21/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/sycl/ink_sy_common.h` (+8/-1)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/sycl/ink_sy_e2m1.h` (+0/-31)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/sycl/ink_sy_ops.h` (+112/-67)
  - `engine/tests/core/sy_e2m1_test.cpp` (+0/-38)

- Связанные решения:
  - `expert-harness`: ours — Сохранить fork CTest/harness; upstream additions объединены без удаления sub8-off проверки.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
On the Arc Pro B70 a decode step spends 16.5 ms of 45 in the attention-residual mix / loop-controller phase (10.6 ms) and the router phase
(5.9 ms): kernels that run as one work-group (or a handful) per token, so one Xe core of 32 does the work and the step waits on its latency.
Every change below keeps the arithmetic of each value, so the logits do not move (checked bit for bit).

- k_ctrl_apply_norm_sg16: the gated mix runs one thread per channel over D/64 work-groups (the same 64-term dots in the same order); the RMS
  norm is a second kernel, one group per token, adding the squares in the order the single kernel did, then wg_sum16.
- k_attn_res_mix_sg16: one work-group per (token, query) instead of one per token (the queries are independent; each repeats the cheap block
  norms), and the block norms and the block dot products are reduced in one batch each (wg_sum16_multi: the same reduce / local sum / reduce
  per value, two barriers for all of them instead of two per value).
- k_router_topk8_sg16: the eight rounds of "best remaining expert, lowest index among equals" run on the 128 threads of the group with exact
  max / min reductions, instead of one thread scanning 8 x 128 entries.
- k_linear_f32_sg16: with up to 1,024 rows (the loop controllers' 64-row projections, the router's 128 rows, the conv taps) each row is one
  sub-group in its own work-group, so the rows spread over the whole GPU instead of N/16 groups; the arithmetic of a row is unchanged.
- The FP4 decode by integer ops is dropped: on the B70 it was 1.5-2.5% slower than the table.
- CI: the speed job also checks identical answers (logits of 64 ids and 48 greedy tokens, base against branch, two runs each).

Arc A750 (p1006, UD-IQ1_S, no XMX): base and branch give the same logits hash (2780509b400ba29d) and the same greedy hash in 4 runs.
```

### `ba6526808412` — CUDA #6671: verify-window rows equal the one-token step (ShortConv arithmetic, GEMV tile, attention split count)

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_kernels.cuh` (+44/-22)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_runner.cuh` (+10/-3)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
The tree / chain verify window gave different bits than the same row decoded alone, so
drafter output could differ from --draft off. Per-stage hashes (STRATA_INK_HASH=1,
STRATA_INK_HASH_VISIT=n) against the B=1 steps found three causes:

- k_ink_gemv_multi_bf16: KT was 576 for 2 <= MAX_M <= 8, not a multiple of 128, so K items
  moved between lanes compared with the M=1 2304 tile. KT is now 512.
- k_ink_sconv4_seq / k_ink_sconv4_tree / k_ink_sconv4_batched and the MoE reduce + sconv
  kernels: nvcc contracted the tap sum and the residual add differently in each kernel. The
  arithmetic is now one helper (ink_sconv_step, ink_mlp_sconv_step) written with
  round-to-nearest intrinsics, so no contraction is possible.
- attention split count: the tree verify now uses the one-token split count.

Debug aids: visit-tap hash slots in ink_runner.cuh, determ_hashcmp.py / determ_hashshow.py.

Result on RTX A6000, SQ-20, prompt 600, 40 tokens: 64 of 64 verify rows identical to the
B=1 step at every stage (before: 64 of 64 differing).
```

### `6bdebbedf583` — fix(setup): the Inkling expert caps are rounded up, so a plan that holds every expert in the card never leaves the last ones on the host

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `terminal/setup.py` (+6/-2)
  - `terminal/tests/terminal/test_inkling_fit_free.py` (+19/-2)

- Связанные решения:
  - `q36-intake`: ours — Candidate расширяет SIZES до пяти setup-моделей реальными KAT/Huihui GGUF-заголовками; FILE_SIZES оставляет три официальных имени.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
setup wrote --vram-experts-gb / --ram-experts-gb with "%.2f" of the plan's GiB, rounded to nearest. A plan that fills the card with every expert
sits exactly on the experts' bytes, so any rounding down (or a table that is a little low) cuts the last expert off: rc0 on an RTX 5090, UD-Q4_K_XL,
wrote --vram-experts-gb 14.42 (the table's 15.48 GB; the file's experts are 15.80 GB) and the engine loaded 3034 experts on the card and 38 on the
host, the hybrid path (hyb=1).

Measured on the 5090 (strata-inkling, same binary, drafter off, one request): with the 0.2.20 flags (--vram-experts-gb 15.48) all 3072 experts
resident, prefill 4264 tok/s on a 4096-token prompt, decode 136; with rc0's flags 38 on the host, prefill 3968 (-6.9%), decode 131.6-132.0 (-3.3%);
with the cap written by this commit (14.76 GiB) all 3072 resident again, prefill 4257, decode 131.7-132.0. Greedy tokens are identical in the three
(the host experts are not what changed the fingerprint GRID saw).

- setup.inkling_expert_flags: both caps are rounded UP to the 0.01 GiB the flag carries; a plan with every expert in the card (full_vram) gets 0.05
  GiB of slack (about 11 experts).
- test_inkling_fit_free: no figure is rounded below itself; UD-Q4_K_XL on a 32 GB card gets a cap of at least its real 15.80 GB + 0.05 and less than
  5% more.
```

### `830bbc2da92d` — fix(setup): the Inkling planner gives a GGUF build the smaller dense share on a single CUDA card of compute capability 8.0 or newer (the loader keeps its Q8_0 matrices)

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `terminal/setup.py` (+5/-0)
  - `terminal/strata_control/inkling_fit.py` (+44/-26)
  - `terminal/tests/terminal/test_inkling_fit_dense.py` (+84/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - `q36-intake`: ours — Candidate расширяет SIZES до пяти setup-моделей реальными KAT/Huihui GGUF-заголовками; FILE_SIZES оставляет три официальных имени.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
INKSPEED's c60259fa6 keeps a GGUF's Q8_0 attention matrices and the embedding as the file stores them (int8 tensor cores) instead of expanding them
to BF16, on one CUDA card of sm_80+ with no layer split; the load line's trunk= falls from 3.93 GB to about 2.9 GB. Every other case (older card,
layer split, other backend, unknown card) still expands to BF16. The planner's GGUF dense share has to follow the card class.

- inkling_fit.dense_gb_for(build, backend, sm, split): "dense_gb_q8" for a GGUF build when the backend is named "cuda", the compute capability is
  known and >= 80, and there is no layer split (extra_vram_gib == 0); "dense_gb" otherwise (an unknown card gets the larger, safe share). sm is a
  new optional argument of compute / place / fits / recommend / rows / max_context / parallel_fits / max_parallel; setup.inkling_plan_extra passes
  the card's compute capability.
- The two shares are what strata-inkling placed on the card with the planner's cap lifted (--vram-experts-gb 50, drafter off, ctx 32768, one NVFP4
  expert = 4.479 MB): BF16: RTX 3060 Ti 7.66 GiB free 2.24 GB, RTX 3060 11.63 GiB free 6.49 GB -> dense_gb 2.45; Q8_0 (dev14 = c60259fa6 on this
  tree): 3060 Ti 703 / 721 experts = 3.19 GB, 3060 1663 / 1681 = 7.49 GB (UD-IQ4_XS / UD-Q4_K_XL) -> dense_gb_q8 1.60 (1.62 and 1.58 from the two
  cards). The plan with the screen reserve equals the engine's capacity within 0.12 GB on both cards and both builds.
- Measured with the same plans, the Q8_0 path also places 36 / 30 more experts and decodes faster on the two cards (UD-IQ4_XS 13.6 -> 17.4 tok/s on
  8 GB, 11.5 -> 14.2 on 12 GB, plans capped as before).
- test_inkling_fit_dense.py: plan == placed experts for both classes, the class table (sm 80 / 86 / 120 take Q8, unknown / 61 / 70 / 75 / split / HIP /
  SYCL / Metal / .strata packs do not), an unknown card never gets the smaller share, setup passes sm.
```

### `3cab928391fa` — fix(launch): the mmproj-BF16.gguf beside an Inkling GGUF is not handed to the engine as its picture reader (#6643 #6597)

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `terminal/strata_cli/launch/adopt.py` (+6/-1)
  - `terminal/tests/terminal/test_inkling_gguf_import.py` (+27/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
An Unsloth GGUF folder carries mmproj-BF16.gguf, llama.cpp's picture reader. launch/adopt.py used it as --vision for a GGUF without a Vision shard.
strata-inkling reads only Inkling-2-Mini-Vision.strata there: given a GGUF, `--info` prints "vision shard: Invalid .strata magic (expected
STRATA\x00\x01)" and images=0 (rc0 engine, RTX 5090, the folder GRID used); the same model with the Vision.strata gives images=1. So a start with the
folder's own mmproj either stopped with "Invalid .strata magic" (the message of #6643 / #6597, which I could not reproduce with `--native <gguf>`
alone: the model was never the file the engine refused) or, since the Terminal probes first, dropped the reader and printed "this engine does not
read images yet", which is not the reason.

- adopt.plan: the GGUF's mmproj*.gguf is never passed as --vision; with one beside the model a note says why and what is used: "mmproj-BF16.gguf
  next to the model is a llama.cpp picture reader that Inkling-2-Mini's engine cannot read; Strata uses Inkling-2-Mini-Vision.strata (0.64 GB) for
  pictures and downloads it when you turn pictures on." A Vision.strata in the model folder or the data directory is used as before.
- test_inkling_gguf_import: a GGUF folder with an mmproj gives no --vision and the note; the Vision shard, once present, is the --vision.
```

### `540f3b3dfbb0` — inkling: the governor also watches the sampled block step, and the probe decodes its chat prompt sampled

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/ink_serve.h` (+17/-14)
  - `terminal/strata_control/inkling_probe.py` (+4/-1)
  - `terminal/tests/terminal/test_inkling_probe.py` (+12/-2)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
Measured 2026-11-23 (RTX A6000, SQ-20, temperature 0.7 top_p 0.95 top_k 64): a sampled request takes the block-8 step, not the greedy tree
step, and the governor only watched the tree step: chat 0.91x and prose 0.92x of plain decoding stayed unprotected (greedy chat with the
governor was 1.04x). The governor now counts the sampled block step too (one gov_step helper for both). The launch probe decodes its code
prompt greedy and its chat prompt sampled the way a chat client asks, so a card that only wins on greedy code is not switched on by a chat
number it will not see.
```

### `6ef0b4693b5b` — fix(inkling2): a drafter file in a layout the engine cannot read is dropped with one message; it never stops the model

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/CMakeLists.txt` (+4/-0)
  - `engine/include/strata/core/ink_dspark_layout.hpp` (+41/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/ink_gguf_loader.h` (+18/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/ink_safetensors_loader.h` (+16/-0)
  - `engine/tests/core/ink_dspark_layout_test.cpp` (+171/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - `expert-harness`: ours — Сохранить fork CTest/harness; upstream additions объединены без удаления sub8-off проверки.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
2026-11-23 14:54 UTC unsloth/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF re-uploaded dspark-Inkling-2-Mini-Q8_0.gguf (402,278,560 -> 503,889,952 bytes) in llama.cpp
mainline's "dflash" layout (commit 19bf97a66719d0165f6f8082a9d59581912a3863 "Support mainline llama.cpp"; the old file stays in the repo as
dspark-Inkling-2-Mini-Q8_0_Old.gguf). Same drafter (3 blocks, 2304 wide, block 8, taps 5 / 23 / 41 / 48, Markov head), written differently:
fuse_weight and the per-block dflare_norm became per-block ctx_mix / ctx_norm, the Markov head's hidden_out projection is folded through the
output head into markov_w2 (+ bias) over the real 200058-token vocabulary, mask_embd has 7 rows, token_embd_norm was added. The engines asked
for the old names and ended the whole start: "missing tensor 'dspark.markov_head.hidden_out.weight'".

strata/core/ink_dspark_layout.hpp: ink_dspark_layout_check() on the plain tensor names a loader collected; the GGUF loader (drafter GGUF and an
external mtp.safetensors) and the official-folder safetensors loader drop the drafter when it fails (drafting off for this start, the arena
space given back), print ink_dspark_layout_message() once (it names the file, what is missing and which files the engine reads), and the model
starts normally. Test ink_dspark_layout_test uses the real tensor lists of the old (54) and the new (58) file.
```

### `ae4bab11b92a` — fix(setup): the Unsloth Inkling GGUF downloads are pinned to the commit the size / sha256 table describes (release blocker)

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `terminal/data/inkling-sources.json` (+2/-2)
  - `terminal/tests/terminal/test_inkling_gguf_pin.py` (+50/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
setup checks every downloaded GGUF against the byte size and SHA-256 in strata_control/inkling_family.py and fetched them from
unsloth/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF resolve/main. On 2026-11-23 14:54 UTC (commit 19bf97a66719d0165f6f8082a9d59581912a3863 "Support mainline llama.cpp")
Unsloth replaced every main GGUF (+1,280 bytes each, a renamed layout: arch inkling2_loop, 24 physical blocks, loop_*_ctrl_* tensors) and the
drafter (402,278,560 -> 503,889,952 bytes, llama.cpp's dflash layout) under the same names. At main 11 of the 13 table entries now differ (the two
mmproj files do not); at commit 800c946d7b9c830c86290df49afbbe91db8455f5, the last commit before it, all 13 match exactly. So every install of an
Unsloth GGUF through setup failed its check.

terminal/data/inkling-sources.json: the GGUF source base is that commit. Overrides (STRATA_INKLING_GGUF_SOURCE, inkling_gguf_source) still win.
tests/terminal/test_inkling_gguf_pin.py: the shipped base is a 40-hex commit, every GGUF url goes through it, the table is the one measured against it.
The desktop app has no table of its own: it starts `setup` (app/host/server/native-control.mjs installArgs), so it is pinned the same way.
```

### `e076650c5c09` — ci(intel-runner): split the SYCL decode "mix" and "router" profiler groups per kernel, and a short inkmix job on the Arc Pro B70

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `.github/ci/inkspeed/b70_mixsplit.sh` (+72/-0)
  - `.github/workflows/intel-runner.yml` (+28/-2)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/sycl/ink_sy_common.h` (+26/-5)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/sycl/ink_sy_runner.h` (+12/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
INK_SY_PROF=2 adds finer marks inside the mix and router groups of a single-token step: residual copy, attention-residual mix, loop-controller
concat / down linear / apply, norm, router gate linear (fx_* in the summary line, with the number of marks per step and the measured cost of an
empty wait(), so the wait overhead of the marks can be subtracted). INK_SY_PROF=1 and the default are unchanged.

New workflow choice job=inkmix runs .github/ci/inkspeed/b70_mixsplit.sh: UD-Q4_K_XL only, HEAD against 5ef71af9b, two alternating C1 pairs, the
profiler at levels 1 and 2, and the identical-answers check (logits of 64 ids twice, 48 greedy tokens of 96 ids twice).

Compiles for spir64 + acm_g10 on the A750 box; INK_SY_PROF=0/1/2 run there with the same decode rate.
```

  - `q36-intake`: ours — Candidate расширяет SIZES до пяти setup-моделей реальными KAT/Huihui GGUF-заголовками; FILE_SIZES оставляет три официальных имени.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
Measured 2026-11-23 on boston (RTX A6000, CUDA 13.1, the same engine and flags): UD-Q4_K_XL at the pinned commit (800c946d..., sha256 e62d463c...)
against the file Unsloth serves from main now (17,629,760,736 bytes, sha256 e64276656f07...), teacher-forced over 2000 tokens of documentation text:
KL 0.000000, top-1 100.00 percent, perplexity 882.151 in both, and again 882.151 on a second run of the new file (noise floor 0). Also the same
first-chat and needle answers with the drafter off, and the new file loads and drafts with the old drafter.

inkling_family.ALT_GGUF_FILES lists the new size and sha256 of the ten main GGUFs (each +1,280 bytes); pins_for(name) gives every (bytes, sha256) a file may
have. setup.inkling_have / inkling_verify accept a file that matches either one (the file's own pin is used for its check). Downloads still go
to the pinned commit. The re-uploaded drafter (503,889,952 bytes, dflash layout) is not listed: the engine drops it with a message.
Tests: test_inkling_gguf_pin.py (both layouts known, the drafter has one, setup accepts either size, rejects another).
```

### `26d8e120da9f` — inkling2/metal: prompt-end checkpoint, so a chat resumes from its last prompt

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/metal/ink_metal_backend.mm` (+92/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/metal/test_metal_prompt_ckpt_live.py` (+128/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/test_metal_ckpt_contract.py` (+54/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
The Metal backend kept the default save/restore_prompt_checkpoint (false), so
the scheduler never found a checkpoint. A chat whose last turn ends in hidden
thinking or a tool call never matches the whole-stream prefix, and every turn
read its whole history again: the 0.2.21 release grid measured a median prompt
reuse of 0% in the agent session on M5 Max (CUDA and HIP: 99.9%).

save_prompt_checkpoint keeps what generation overwrites after the prompt: the
ShortConv histories, the SWA rings of the 40 sliding-window visits, the
drafter's latest f_rnn and its two ring context layers. Global KV below the
checkpoint is never overwritten. restore puts it back and drops the verify /
tree rollback state. alloc_slot, free_slot and reset_slot drop the checkpoint.

Tests: test_metal_ckpt_contract.py (source contract, fails without the change),
metal/test_metal_prompt_ckpt_live.py (real engine on a Mac: reuse counts and
resumed vs cold greedy tokens).
```

- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_cuda_backend.cu` (+2/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_hybrid.cuh` (+50/-15)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_runner.cuh` (+50/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
STRATA_INK_EXACT is now unset by default: after the runner exists, a short launch probe (24 real
token ids, 18 timed decode steps per lane, tier paused, usage counters reset afterwards) times the
CPU lane and the card's own copy-in lane on the placement the loaders made, keeps the CPU lane
unless the copy-in lane is at least 10% faster, and logs one INFO line with both times.
STRATA_INK_EXACT=1 forces the copy-in lane (identical answers wherever an expert lives, PCIe
bound), =0 forces the CPU lane. set_lane() switches between them; the staging buffers of the exact
lane are prepared whenever the arena is pinned so that the probe can time it.

The CPU lane's host evaluator treated GGUF Q8_0 experts as "no activation kernel" (the weight type
equals its activation type), so they were dequantised to float and summed by a scalar loop, one
expert per thread (the 8.2 MB class of UD-Q4_K_XL). They now use the Q8_0 x Q8_0 dot kernels and are
shared by rows like the other formats: UD-Q4_K_XL on a 12 GB card 16 -> 27 tok/s at an 8 GiB plan.

Also: per-visit profile of the row-shared CPU path under STRATA_INK_CPU_PROF.
```

### `accfd7ace3e6` — inkling2: AVX-512 for the fast lane's CPU experts, and run-time AVX2 / AVX-512 tiers for the S_K / SF4 / MX8 codecs

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/cmake/backends/quant.cmake` (+31/-2)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/CMakeLists.txt` (+57/-1)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_hybrid.cuh` (+16/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/ink_host_avx2.cpp` (+65/-53)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/ink_host_avx512.cpp` (+211/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/ink_host_avx512.h` (+23/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/ink_host_avx512_gate.cpp` (+21/-0)
  - `engine/src/quant/sk_codecs.cpp` (+119/-7)
  - `engine/src/quant/sk_codecs_base.cpp` (+4/-0)
  - `engine/src/quant/sk_dispatch.cpp` (+80/-0)
  - `engine/src/quant/sk_tiers.hpp` (+34/-0)
  - `engine/src/quant/x86/sk_codecs_avx2.cpp` (+5/-0)
  - `engine/src/quant/x86/sk_codecs_avx512.cpp` (+5/-0)
  - `engine/tests/core/ink_host_simd_bench.cpp` (+98/-0)
  - `engine/tests/core/ink_host_simd_test.cpp` (+272/-0)
  - `engine/tests/quant/sk_tier_bench.cpp` (+77/-0)
  - `engine/tests/quant/sk_tier_test.cpp` (+191/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
1. CUDA fast lane (cold experts computed on the CPU): new ink_host_avx512.cpp has the three host kernels (SF4 row, MX8 row, S1.5..S8_K sub-group) for
   AVX-512 F/DQ/BW/VL (no VNNI, so Skylake-X runs it too). The file is built with the AVX-512 flags and nothing else is; its gate, host_avx512::available(),
   is in ink_host_avx512_gate.cpp, a baseline-flag file (a compiler may use AVX-512 anywhere in a file built with -mavx512f, so the gate cannot live there):
   caps().avx512, closed by STRATA_FORCE_ISA=avx2. ink_hybrid.cuh tries AVX-512, then AVX2, then plain C++.
   ink_host_avx2.cpp unpacked the S2_K / S3_K / S5_K / S6_K fields with scalar loops (0.7 to 1.1 GB/s of weights per thread): shuffles now, integer sums exact.

2. The CPU backend and the HIP / SYCL CPU-expert lane (eval_inkling2_expert_batch -> sk_codecs.cpp) ran plain x86-64 C++: strata_quant builds sk_codecs.cpp with
   no ISA flag (its AVX2 / AVX-512 code is selected by __AVX2__ at build time). It is now compiled three times (sk_codecs_base.cpp, x86/sk_codecs_avx2.cpp,
   x86/sk_codecs_avx512.cpp) into strata::quant::sk::{base,avx2,avx512} and sk_dispatch.cpp picks the tier from caps() (AVX-512 needs VNNI there, as strata_quant's
   own tier does). A CPU without AVX2 never executes an AVX2 instruction of it, and a -march=native host cannot leak wide code into the base tier. Tier files are
   -ffp-contract=off: the integer sums are exact and the float steps are the base tier's, so every S_K result is bit-identical across tiers (the aarch64 path and the
   builds that compile sk_codecs.cpp themselves (hy4flash, Metal, the SYCL script) are unchanged). AVX2 gets vector unpackers and an abs/sign int8 dot.
   SF4 / MX8 sum in lane order, so they differ from the scalar tier by float rounding.

Tests: tests/core/ink_host_simd_test.cpp (all formats, scalar reference, AVX2 and AVX-512, F8_E4M3 decode on all 256 codes), tests/quant/sk_tier_test.cpp (tiers
against each other: S_K bit-identical, dispatcher = reported tier), benches ink_host_simd_bench / sk_tier_bench. Run on Zen 4 and Zen 5 (AVX-512 + VNNI), Zen 2 and under
qemu -cpu Nehalem / SandyBridge / IvyBridge (gates closed, nothing executed above the CPU's level), tools/check --only cmake-cpu: 160 passed.

One thread, S_K gemm of a 2304 x 2304 expert matrix, one token, base -> avx2 (Zen 4): S2_K 10x, S3_K 13x, S4_K 2.9x, S5_K 9x, S6_K 8x, S8_K 2.7x. AVX-512 over AVX2: 1.0x on
Zen 4, 1.0 to 1.7x on Zen 5 (ink_host kernels: SF4 1.57x, MX8 1.69x, S3_K 1.35x, S5_K 1.5x).
```

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
materializeSkills removed every folder in the agent skills folder that was
not in the current skill list, so a skill a person kept there was gone after
an update. Now Strata keeps a note (.strata-skills.json) of the folders it
wrote, and only those, or folders holding its own .strata-copied.json copy
note, are ever taken away. They are moved to skills-removed next to the
folder instead of deleted, so a skill whose source was missing for a moment
can be put back. A skill whose name a person's folder already has is written
under another name. A 0.2.20 layout (no note yet) is read once: its bundled
skills are updated in place, its folders with a copy note are Strata's, every
other folder is the person's.

Tests: skill-live-6857.test.mjs (person's skill without a marker survives
several syncs; upgrade from the 0.2.20 layout; unreadable note; name clash).
agent-skills.test.mjs no longer expects a hand-made folder to be removed.
```

### `d9d5854323e3` — perf(inkling2/sycl): one launch for the three loop-controller down linears, loads of the small F32 linears hoisted, no separate residual copies, bit for bit the same results

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/sycl/ink_sy_codecs.h` (+48/-13)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/sycl/ink_sy_ops.h` (+5/-1)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/sycl/ink_sy_runner.h` (+29/-10)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
The B70 per-kernel split (run 45235211954, UD-Q4_K_XL) showed the loop-controller down linear ([64 x 4608] F32, 96 launches of 69 us per decode step, 6.6 ms),
the 9 KB residual copies (96 d2d calls of 32 us, 3.1 ms) and the router gate linear (48 launches of 39 us) as the largest small items of a step.

- k_linear_f32_sg16 (rows <= 1024) and the new k_linear_f32x3_sg16 share f32_row_dot_sg16: the loads of 8 consecutive products of a lane are issued
  together, the multiply-adds run in the same ascending-k order per lane and the sub-group sum is unchanged, so every value is bit for bit the old one;
  a row no longer waits for a memory round trip per product.
- The attn / k / v controllers of a visit are independent (each concat reads its own stream and message, each apply writes its own stream): three
  concats, one launch of the three down linears (3 x 64 work-groups), three applies. The old per-controller path stays for other tensor formats.
- k_attn_res_mix_sg16 can also write its current-stream input to the residual buffer, which replaces the separate d2d copy before the attention
  mix and before the MoE mix (layer 0 has no mix before attention and keeps its copy). b_cat / b_ctrl_gate hold one region per controller.

Gate (Arc A750, UD-IQ1_S, SYCL, no XMX difference between arms): logits of 64 ids sha 2780509b400ba29d in all four runs (base cm-mix1 = e076650c5,
new, base, new), 48 greedy tokens of 96 ids identical in all four runs. The Arc Pro B70 run (job=inkmix) follows.
```

```
Unsloth re-uploaded its drafter in another layout on 2026-11-23, and setup depended on that one file name. The original checkpoint is public
(thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini, Apache-2.0, not gated: anonymous curl, HTTP 206 on a ranged GET, no token), unchanged since the upload commit
1fb4134b9a74f9681054f4ef82e4bf1f458a2337 (later commits only touch README / config).

inkling_family: MTP_FILE / MTP_BASE (the commit URL) / DRAFTER_FILES (635,801,416 bytes, sha256 7c3b6513...a1d2), drafter_sources (config
inkling_drafter_source, env STRATA_INKLING_DRAFTER_SOURCE, STRATA_INKLING_SOURCE mirror, then the pinned repository); size_of / sha256_of / pins_for know it.
setup.inkling_fetch_drafter: an install that already has a complete drafter keeps it (no second download); otherwise mtp.safetensors (636 MB, the size
is printed), and when it cannot be fetched or does not check out, Unsloth's pinned dspark-Inkling-2-Mini-Q8_0.gguf (402 MB) with a warning, without
a "Setup stopped" or an error event. inkling_find_local_dspark prefers a local mtp.safetensors over a dspark*.gguf (which may be the new layout).
The planner's drafter file size is 0.636 GB (unified-memory fit, disk, download size).

Measured 2026-11-23 on an RTX A6000 (CUDA 12.8, UD-Q4_K_XL, same engine, 2 rounds, chain and tree unchanged): the original and Unsloth's old Q8_0 drafter
give the same acceptance (tokens per step code 3.6 / 3.6, edit 5.6 / 5.6, chat 1.9 / 1.9, json 3.7 / 3.6, count 5.7 / 5.7, tool 4.6 / 4.6, doc4k 2.6 / 2.8)
and the same speed within noise (x off: code 1.27 / 1.29, edit 1.85 / 1.88, chat 0.93 / 0.94, count 2.17 / 2.15). Both take 416 MiB on the card ("DSpark took
416 MiB" with either, free memory after load identical to the MiB): the engine holds the matrices as BF16 in both cases, so the card size does not decide.
Tensor by tensor against the original: Unsloth's Q8_0 file is bit-equal in every F32 / BF16 tensor and 0.55 percent relative RMS in the 2-D matrices.
```

### `e6c2d002e276` — fix(cuda): the sm_70 table's STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1 yields to the 12-token lookup window (#6747)

- Дата: 2026-11-23

  - `engine/src/core/nv_defaults.cpp` (+3/-1)
  - `engine/src/core/nv_defaults_test.cpp` (+47/-0)
  - `engine/src/program/generate.cpp` (+23/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
The V100 table (0.2.20) sets STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1, which holds kVerifyMaxT (8) rows per
thread and has no batched commit. The 8-row CUDA build's default --lookup-max-t is 12,
so the first request formed a 12-token window and gdn_step_norm_multi ended the engine
("invalid arguments", HTTP 503, restart loop under a supervisor).

Once the lookup default is resolved, generate.cpp now settles the pair
(gdn_split_window_fix): the table's switch is dropped with one line (the wide window
stays, as before the sm_70 table existed); a STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1 the user set is kept and
the lookup window is clamped to the build's rows with a warning. A 16-row build keeps
the split (it has no default lookup window).

nv_defaults_test gets the table-consistency check: for every compute capability, card
size, STRATA_DEFAULTS and build width (8 / 12 / 16 rows) the settled configuration never
pairs the split with a window wider than the build. docs/NVIDIA_V100.md says so.

Test: nv_defaults_test, adapt_fetch_default_test (p2006). Not run on a V100 (none left).
```

### `e3a920f4dfc8` — engine: native_mmvq.hpp includes <cstdint> (#6837)

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/include/strata/kernels/native_mmvq.hpp` (+1/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
The header uses int8_t and included only <cstddef>, so a translation unit that
reaches it before anything pulls in <cstdint> does not compile (GCC 15 on Arch
and Fedora 42+ with the test suite on: q8_gemv_bench).

Checked on p2006 (g++ 13.3, a translation unit whose first include is the
header, -fsyntax-only): fails with "int8_t does not name a type" without the
include, compiles with it.
```

### `fc28199bfd26` — app: a new skill keeps the workspace it was created for (Skills > New skill > Available in)

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `app/host/server/index.mjs` (+10/-4)
  - `app/host/src/screens/Skills.tsx` (+8/-1)
  - `app/host/tests/split-qa2-skills.test.mjs` (+8/-1)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
The workspace chosen under Available in was dropped on Save, so the skill
showed under All workspaces until it was edited again. The create request now
carries it, the host checks it the way the edit route does (an unknown
workspace is refused before any file is written) and keeps it with the skill's
other preferences, so it survives a reload and a restart. A request without a
workspace keeps All workspaces.

From PR #6884 by @DivyamTalwar (the diff was scanned for secrets first). One
change: an empty value counts as All workspaces, as in the edit route.
Test: split-qa2-skills.test.mjs (the scope, restart, a missing workspace).
```

```
strata launch adopting prepared model files rewrote the installed run config

```

### `107df67e3013` — app: test that picking or adopting a model never fetches a newer engine over the chosen one (#6875)

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `app/host/tests/packaged-control.test.mjs` (+24/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
The engine chosen in Settings > Engine is pinned; the install job's engine step
(the same job for a download and for the person's own GGUF folder) leaves a
pinned engine alone since rc0 (9d80fb2e4, 5907fe7ff, #6830). The reporter's
case on 0.2.18 to 0.2.20 was this path. packaged-control.test.mjs now runs
both jobs (a model to download, and a GGUF folder) against a feed that offers a
newer engine: with a chosen engine the updater is not called and the message
says the chosen engine stays in use; with no pin the engine still follows the
feed with the model.
The test fails on f65f2d614 (0.2.20 plus fixes) and passes on rc1.
```

### `8500b11adf15` — update: the test start names the run config it used and the env settings in it; tests that the config env reaches the engine (#6868)

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `terminal/strata_control/updater.py` (+4/-0)
  - `terminal/tests/terminal/test_updater.py` (+57/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
The report says the update's test start ignores the run config's "env", so the
two #6713 workaround lines put there do nothing. It does not: the test start
writes the config's env (plus its own STRATA_PLE_AUTO_RAM=0) into the sandbox
config, and serve.server gives exactly that env to the engine, over the shell's.
Tests (test_updater.RunConfigEnvInTheTestStart): the sandbox config and
serve.server.child_env; and the whole path with nothing mocked (real runtime,
real server, a stub engine that writes its environment) with the opposite
values exported in the shell. Both pass without a code change.

What can differ is which config is tested: one config only, the one a saved
profile or launch preset uses, else the first installed model's by id. So the
test start now says, when that config has an env, "Testing engine <version>
with the run config <file>, with its environment settings <names>".
```

### `439498d4fa12` — setup: the drafter file follows what the installed engine can read (--info line flag dspark_f32_widen=1)

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/ink_main.cpp` (+1/-1)
  - `terminal/serve/inkling_kind.py` (+27/-0)
  - `terminal/setup.py` (+30/-15)
  - `terminal/strata_control/inkling_family.py` (+10/-0)
  - `terminal/tests/terminal/test_inkling_gguf_pin.py` (+66/-5)
  - `terminal/tests/terminal/test_inkling_unsloth_4gb.py` (+3/-2)

- Связанные решения:
  - `q36-intake`: ours — Candidate расширяет SIZES до пяти setup-моделей реальными KAT/Huihui GGUF-заголовками; FILE_SIZES оставляет три официальных имени.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
Measured 2026-11-23 on a Mac (M5 Max, Metal, UD-Q4_K_XL): an engine without the BF16 -> F32 widen of the drafter's norms and biases gets 1.0 tokens per step from
mtp.safetensors (every draft rejected, 0.5 to 0.9x speed) while Unsloth's Q8_0 file gives 3.3 to 7.6 on the same build; with the widen both files give the same
acceptance and speed. Users keep older engines (0.1.63 / 0.1.65, the GUI engine picker), so setup must not assume the newest one.

engine: the `--info <model>` line ends with dspark_f32_widen=1 (ink_main.cpp). Builds without the commit do not print it.
inkling_family: ENGINE_MTP_FLAG, engine_reads_mtp(info).
setup: inkling_engine_reads_mtp(engine, model, lib_dirs) runs the engine's --info once (serve.inkling_kind.probe, cached) on the downloaded main GGUF; the flag
decides, not the version, and an engine that is missing, does not run or says nothing counts as one that cannot. inkling_fetch_drafter(reads_mtp): an engine that
reads it gets the original mtp.safetensors (or the file the install already has), with Unsloth's pinned Q8_0 as the fallback; an engine that does not gets
Unsloth's pinned Q8_0 only, and an mtp.safetensors already on disk stays there and is not passed. inkling_find_local_dspark(folder, reads_mtp) does the same for
files the person already has (a folder with only the original and an engine that cannot read it: no drafter, drafting off).
serve.inkling_kind.fit_dspark (called in engine_args after the --info probe): a run config that names mtp.safetensors but is started with an engine that does not
list the flag (an older engine picked later) passes the Q8_0 file beside it, or with none starts without a drafter; the launch probe stays the judge of on/off.
Tests: test_inkling_gguf_pin.py (15 tests: the flag, setup on both paths, local folders, fit_dspark, engine_args with and without the flag).
```

### `c25b0fdddd7f` — inkling2 CPU backend: AVX2 / AVX-512 / NEON dense dot, and matmul parallel over the weight rows

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/include/strata/quant/sk_codecs.hpp` (+4/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/ink_cpu_backend.cpp` (+12/-17)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/inkling2_loop.cpp` (+1/-11)
  - `engine/src/quant/sk_codecs.cpp` (+51/-0)
  - `engine/src/quant/sk_dispatch.cpp` (+3/-1)
  - `engine/src/quant/sk_tiers.hpp` (+1/-0)
  - `engine/tests/quant/sk_tier_test.cpp` (+18/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
The q / k / v / o / gate projections of the CPU backend (matmul_f32) were `parallel for` over the activation rows with `if (M * N >= 4096)`: a one-token decode step
ran most of them on ONE thread, and a prompt read every weight row M times from memory. They are parallel over the weight rows now (threshold on M * N * K), each row is
read once and reused for all M activation rows from L1; every y[m][n] is the same dot call as before, so the result does not depend on the thread count.

The dot itself (CPU backend, attention scores, inkling2_loop.cpp's helpers) is strata::quant::sk::dot_f32, one more function of the run-time tiers: 4 accumulators of the
tier's vector width (AVX-512 / AVX2 with FMA / NEON), plain 4-accumulator C++ in the base tier (bit-identical to the sum it replaces: sk_tier_test checks it). The vector
tiers sum in lane order, so a CPU-only run differs from 0.2.20 by float rounding (SQ-10 teacher-forced KL(old||new) 4e-4, repeatable run to run).

Measured, CPU backend, SQ-10 prefill 128 / decode 8, alternating pairs: Apple M5 Max prefill 3.2 -> 7.7 ppts, decode 1.6 -> 2.5 tok/s (spread under 1 %);
Zen 4 16 threads, UD-Q2_K_XL: prefill 11.1 -> 13.0, decode 2.7 -> 4.3.
```

### `dca06a36df5e` — fix(serve): the watchdog's limits are parsed without undefined behaviour and its message prints the real wait (#6861)

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/CMakeLists.txt` (+5/-0)
  - `engine/include/strata/core/watchdog_limits.hpp` (+31/-0)
  - `engine/src/core/watchdog_limits_test.cpp` (+28/-0)
  - `engine/src/program/generate.cpp` (+11/-6)

- Связанные решения:
  - `expert-harness`: ours — Сохранить fork CTest/harness; upstream additions объединены без удаления sub8-off проверки.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
STRATA_WATCHDOG_S and STRATA_WATCHDOG_IO_S were read with std::atoi. The #6861 logs show
"no progress for -1195029860 s" and "no step finished for -1907795513 s ... waiting up to
2079576072 s": a negative or garbage limit makes the first silent second count as stuck and
shortens the file-tier allowance (the engine was stopped after about 10-19 s instead of 60).

watchdog_seconds() (strata/core/watchdog_limits.hpp) parses with strtol: an unparsable or
out-of-range value (negative, past a week, past long) falls back to the default and the
engine says so. The "no progress" line prints the seconds actually waited.
watchdog_limits_test covers the values atoi turned into garbage.

This does not cure a real stall: the reporter's later runs with a limit of 60 also stop at
layer step 1 of the last prompt chunk. That hang was not reproduced on an RTX 5070 (sm_120,
WDDM) with his flags, a control vector, --slots 2 and --adapt-async 1.
```

### `6e45f7fbd3c5` — fix(cuda): the expert cache on Windows WDDM prices what the load really allocates after it (#6836 #6887 #6509 #6846)

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/include/strata/core/low_vram_rules.hpp` (+7/-1)
  - `engine/src/core/low_vram_rules_test.cpp` (+3/-1)
  - `engine/src/program/generate.cpp` (+19/-2)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
0.1.66 priced 384 MiB for "what is allocated after the cache" on WDDM (256 before) and added
a shrink-after-write loop that wanted reserve + draft head + 384 MiB free once the slots were
written. Since 0.1.65 the BF16/FP16 GEMM warm-up (about 180 MiB of cuBLAS workspace) runs
BEFORE the cache is sized, so only the verifier's buffers and graph captures come after it.
Measured on an RTX 5070 12 GB (Windows, IQ3_S pack, MTP, spec 4): 134 MiB at --vram-reserve-mib
300, 110 MiB at 700, 126 MiB at 1536. The card ended with 606-620 MiB free (reserve 300) and
the cache lost 0.36 GiB against 0.1.65 (2287 -> 2099 slots, 4.40 -> 4.04 GiB): the 886 -> 562
experts of #6836 on an 8 GB laptop, 3598 -> 3204 slots in the #6713 table, 7.63 vs 8.38 GiB
of #6846.

kWddmLateAllocMib 384 -> 192 (measured plus 50-80 MiB for a wider window), and the shrink loop's
slack under WDDM 0 -> 32 MiB (the slot count rounds down, so the free figure is a few MiB under
the need by construction: 902 against 904 MiB cost a 64 MiB shrink and a second cache write).
Result on the same card: 2232 slots (4.29 GiB), 360 MiB free at the end (the engine's own
paging threshold is 256 MiB; the 8 GB laptop's 0.1.62 ran at 336 MiB, a forced 250 MiB paged).

The start-up now prints what the load took after the cache against what was priced ("after the
expert cache was written N MiB were free; M MiB were taken since ..."), so the price can be
checked on any card from one log.

Tests: low_vram_rules_test (the price, and that it never exceeds the plain rule's).
```

### `64c224f3c1d6` — inkling HIP: size the SWA KV ring for the batch span (wrong logits past 1024 tokens, #6878); --ring-check

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/hip/ink_hip_backend.hip.cpp` (+77/-25)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/hip/ink_hip_ops.hip.h` (+15/-15)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/hip/ink_hip_test.hip.cpp` (+1/-1)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/hip/ink_hip_tree.hip.h` (+6/-6)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/ink_main.cpp` (+87/-1)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
From PR #6879 by @jbox5.

forward_batch_chunk stores the K/V of every token of a batch before attention reads the ring, and the ring held exactly swa_win = 1024
positions, so a batch that reaches past position 1024 overwrote keys its own earlier tokens still need (prompts over 1024 tokens, prefill
chunks crossing 1024, linear DSpark verify batches). The ring is now swa_win + max(chunk, 64) positions in whole 64-token pages, forward_batch
splits a batch at the margin when a slot's ring wraps, and the attention, store, page-index and tree-commit code take the ring size next to the
window (STRATA_INK_SWA_RING=N overrides it; N = 1024 brings the old ring back for A/B checks).

Merged onto rc1: the expert-arena budget keeps the free-VRAM clamp (#6711) and counts the extra ring bytes of each slot; the #6671 exact-rows
tree split-KV kernel takes the ring size; the prompt-checkpoint comments describe the ring size.

New: strata-inkling --ring-check STRIDE --prompt-ids ...: the prompt run as batches (INK_RING_CHECK_BATCH tokens, default 4096) against the
same prompt one token per forward, KL and top-1 at every STRIDE-th position and after the window. The one-token steps never overwrote a key,
so they are the reference on every backend; a ring overwrite shows as KL of order 1 and a top-1 agreement far below 90%.
```

### `5281882cf0cf` — perf(inkling2/cuda): batched SF4 / MX8 expert kernel for sm_80..89 that reads each expert once at memory speed, bit for bit the same results

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_moe_cuda.cuh` (+292/-2)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_runner.cuh` (+2/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
For 24 or more tokens per step (32 / 64 concurrent requests, prefill chunks) on sm_80..89 the SF4 / MX8 experts ran k_ink_moe_sf4_mx8_fp16tc. It loaded 2 KB
of weights per block and step (one 16-byte load per thread), staged them through shared memory behind two barriers per 32 values of K and had nothing in
flight while it computed: a visit cost about 3x what reading the experts costs (RTX A6000, 32 slots).

k_ink_moe_fp16tc_v2<GU, FMT> (SF4 and MX8): every warp decodes the weights of its own 16 rows straight into the mma fragments, with no shared weights and
no barriers in the K loop; one group of 32-value steps is loaded ahead of the one being computed; only the activations are staged (384 values of K at a
time). The arithmetic is the old kernel's operation for operation (SF4: per 16 values of K one mma, then acc = fma(block scale, result, acc); MX8: both
mmas of 32 values accumulate, then one fma with the block scale; K ascending), so the logits are bit for bit those of the old kernel.

It is used for layers whose experts are all SF4 or all MX8 and whose gate/up and down formats match (InkLayerMoeInfo::mixed_gu_dn is set at both places
that fill the layer info); every other layer keeps the old kernel. STRATA_INK_MOE_V1=1 selects the old kernel everywhere. sm_120 keeps its FP4 kernel.

Measured on an RTX A6000 (UD-Q4_K_XL), whole decode step: 32 slots 137 -> 68 ms, 64 slots 181 -> 105 ms (C32 total decode about 2x, C64 about +54%).
Gates (RTX A6000, sm_86): logits of a 400-token sequence fed in chunks of 400 / 64 / 32 / 24 tokens identical to the old kernel (STRATA_INK_MOE_V1=1)
for UD-Q4_K_XL and SQ-20; compute-sanitizer memcheck, racecheck and synccheck, filtered to the new kernel at 32 slots, report 0 errors and 0 hazards on
both models (the SF4 instantiation in UD-Q4_K_XL, SF4 and MX8 in SQ-20).
```

### `eb6db6c9503c` — fix(inkling2/cuda): Blackwell (sm_120 / sm_121) keeps the BF16 dense matrices of a GGUF build, the int8 dense GEMM is slower than BF16 there

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_cuda_backend.cu` (+4/-1)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
INTEG's rc1 first-chat cells on an RTX 5090 (CUDA 13): UD-Q4_K_XL decode 98.4 tok/s against 133 for 0.2.20 with every expert resident, SQ-20 unchanged
(138 against 134). The 5090 phase profile of c60259fa6 says the same: dense QKV 3.51 ms and wo 1.93 ms per decode step for UD-Q4_K_XL against 1.87 / 0.66 ms
for SQ-20 (BF16-class dense), 11.1 ms per step against 7.9. On sm_86 the same path gained +7..10% decode, so the cut is by architecture:
ink_cuda_q8f_supported returns false for compute capability major 12, which gives the BF16 expansion of the Q8_0 matrices and the BF16 embedding (the
behaviour of 0.2.20) on that class. Ampere and Ada (sm_80..89) are unchanged. STRATA_INK_Q8_0_DENSE=0 still forces BF16 everywhere.
The terminal planner takes the same cut in its own commit (Q8_DENSE_MAX_SM), so the dense share it budgets on a Blackwell card is the BF16 one.
```

### `86818d88a7ba` — fix(setup): the Inkling planner budgets the BF16 dense share on Blackwell (sm 120 / 121), where the engine keeps the BF16 matrices

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `terminal/strata_control/inkling_fit.py` (+4/-1)
  - `terminal/tests/terminal/test_inkling_fit_dense.py` (+2/-2)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
The int8 dense GEMM of a GGUF build is slower than BF16 at one token on an RTX 5090 (UD-Q4_K_XL decode 98 against 133 tok/s), so ink_cuda_q8f_supported
in the engine is false for compute capability major 12 and the loader expands the Q8_0 matrices there as in 0.2.20. dense_gb_for gives the smaller Q8_0
share only for 80 <= sm < 120 (Q8_DENSE_MAX_SM), otherwise a Blackwell card would be planned about 0.85 GB too roomy.
Test: sm 120 / 121 take the BF16 share, 80 / 86 / 89 the Q8_0 one.
```

### `8e208f1e6dc6` — fix(inkling2/cuda): the int8 dense GEMM of a GGUF build is used on consumer Ampere (sm_86) only

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_cuda_backend.cu` (+8/-6)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
A/B on an RTX 4090 (sm_89), UD-Q4_K_XL, all experts resident, three alternating rounds, int8 dense (default) against STRATA_INK_Q8_0_DENSE=0:
C1 decode 95.3 / 95.5 / 95.5 against 103.7 / 103.4 / 104.0 tok/s (-8%), C8 333 / 336 / 335 against 330 / 326 / 330 (+1.5%), prefill equal (3,450 against
3,452 ppts), trunk 2.25 against 3.29 GB. With the RTX 5090 result (98 against 133 tok/s at C1) the int8 path wins at one token only on sm_86 (RTX A6000
+7..10%), so ink_cuda_q8f_supported now returns true for compute capability 8.6 only; sm_80 (A100) is unmeasured and stays on BF16. This replaces the
"major != 12" cut of the previous commit. The terminal planner takes the same set in its own commit (Q8_DENSE_SMS).
```

### `cd568d5e2a3a` — fix(setup): the Inkling planner budgets the smaller Q8_0 dense share on sm 86 only

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `terminal/strata_control/inkling_fit.py` (+4/-5)
  - `terminal/tests/terminal/test_inkling_fit_dense.py` (+1/-3)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
The engine keeps a GGUF build's Q8_0 dense matrices (int8 tensor cores) on compute capability 8.6 only: the int8 GEMM is slower than BF16 at one token on an
RTX 4090 (sm 89, 95.4 against 103.7 tok/s) and an RTX 5090 (sm 120, 98 against 133). dense_gb_for gives dense_gb_q8 only for sm in Q8_DENSE_SMS = (86,), so
the plan matches what the loader keeps; 80, 89, 120 and 121 plan the BF16 share. Test updated.
```

### `66f2ee2b0a4b` — perf(cpu): the 4-row dot kernels of the native expert path are opt-in (#6552)

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/CMakeLists.txt` (+5/-0)
  - `engine/cmake/backends/cpu.cmake` (+4/-0)
  - `engine/include/strata/quant/dot_x4_policy.hpp` (+19/-0)
  - `engine/src/core/dot_x4_policy_test.cpp` (+21/-0)
  - `engine/src/kernels/cpu/native_expert.cpp` (+3/-2)
  - `engine/tests/core/dot_x4_bench.cpp` (+84/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - `expert-harness`: ours — Сохранить fork CTest/harness; upstream additions объединены без удаления sub8-off проверки.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
4414c2988 (0.2.20) put the dot_x4 kernels in front of the 1-row dots in native_gu_rows /
native_down_rows (Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q8_0, IQ4_XS, IQ3_XXS ...), on by default. They give the
same bits (dot_x4_test) and share the activation loads, which pays with the weights in cache.
A cold expert is read from DRAM, and there the 4-row form is slower. New dot_x4_bench (one
thread, 512 MiB of rows, n = 2560), x4 speed against four 1-row calls:
  Ryzen 7 255 (Zen 4, AVX-512 VNNI)  Q4_0 0.77  Q8_0 0.42  Q4_K 0.26  Q5_K 0.33  Q6_K 0.24  IQ4_XS 0.27  IQ3_XXS 0.52
  Ryzen 5 5600X (Zen 3, AVX2)        Q8_0 0.85  Q4_K 0.29  IQ4_XS 0.32
  i9-13900K (AVX-VNNI)               Q8_0 1.20  Q4_K 0.86  IQ4_XS 0.80
  (cache-resident: 0.8 - 1.3 everywhere)
This is the #6552 reporter's Ryzen 7 7700 (STRATA_NO_DOT_X4=1 brought the old speed back).

dot_x4_enabled() (strata/quant/dot_x4_policy.hpp): STRATA_DOT_X4=1 turns the kernels on,
STRATA_NO_DOT_X4 (any value) still turns them off and wins. The answers are the same bits either
way. dot_x4_policy_test covers the rule; dot_x4_bench is registered as an executable only.
```

### `2612ae5c0e4d` — perf(inkling2/cuda): Windows pins the host expert arena up to min(16 GiB, 35% of the available RAM) (was 8 GB), with an 8 GiB floor and STRATA_INK_PIN_GB

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/CMakeLists.txt` (+4/-0)
  - `engine/include/strata/core/ink_pin_rule.hpp` (+49/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_hybrid.cuh` (+13/-3)
  - `engine/tests/core/ink_pin_rule_test.cpp` (+48/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - `expert-harness`: ours — Сохранить fork CTest/harness; upstream additions объединены без удаления sub8-off проверки.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
A pinned arena lets the card read the cold experts itself: the exact lane stages inside the CUDA
graph instead of copying through a pageable arena + bounce ring with one host sync per visit. On the
owner PC (RTX 5070, x16) SQ-10 at an 8 GiB plan goes from 30 to 49 tok/s in that lane, SQ-20 from
8 to 15; the launch probe still picks the lane (pinned exact against the CPU lane).

The rule is a pure function (core/ink_pin_rule.hpp, tested by ink_pin_rule_test): Windows cap
min(16 GiB, 35% of the available RAM), and an arena that would leave under 8 GiB of RAM available is
not pinned; STRATA_INK_PIN_GB=<n> sets the cap in GiB (both platforms), =0 turns pinning off; Linux
keeps its rule (under 45% of the available RAM). When the rule says no, or cudaHostAlloc fails, the
arena is pageable as before, with one INFO line saying why; the start never fails on this.
```

### `7d635fe05142` — perf(inkling2/cuda): the GGUF-stored experts (the Q8_0 layers of the UD files) use 2 tokens per group up to 128 slots, and the int8 tensor cores from 256 tokens

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_moe_cuda.cuh` (+165/-12)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
Four layers of UD-Q4_K_XL have Q8_0 experts (layers 20-23) and run the dp4a kernels k_ink_moe_gu/dn_gguf_dp4a. Above 32 slots they used 16 tokens per group,
which costs far more than reading the weights: for the four layers at 64 slots 14.1 ms on an RTX 5090 (the bytes cost 2.4 ms), 30.9 ms on an RTX A6000,
17.9 ms on an RTX 4090. Two tokens per group (STRATA_INK_GGUF_MT forces 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16) costs 8.0 / 19.9 / 12.7 ms; at 8 slots every setting is equal, at 32 slots
2 is best or tied (A6000 11.4 ms against 13.2 with 4 per group). The dp4a result of a token does not depend on the group size, so the logits are bit for bit those of
the old setting (checked on the A6000 and the 4090).

k_ink_moe_q80_tc runs the same experts on the int8 tensor cores (a warp owns 16 output rows, a group of 8 tokens is the N of one mma.m16n8k32.s8 per 32-value
block). The int32 block sum is exact in both kernels and every (row, token) keeps the dp4a kernel's 8 accumulators (block b into accumulator b % 8, fmaf(d_w * d_x,
sum, acc), blocks ascending) and its reduction tree, so the output is bit for bit the same. It loses at decode batch sizes (64 slots 17.1 ms against 12.7; 8 slots
4.6 against 2.3 on a 4090), so it is used only from 256 tokens (STRATA_INK_Q80_TC = N: from N tokens, 0 never): a 2048-token prefill chunk of UD-Q4_K_XL on an
RTX 4090 goes from 2,805 to 3,370 ppts, and the Q8_0 layers were half of that chunk.

Gates: logits of a 2300-token sequence fed in chunks of 2048 / 1024 / 256 / 128 / 64 and of a 400-token sequence in chunks of 400 / 64 / 32 / 24 / 8 / 2, identical to the
previous tree on an RTX A6000 and an RTX 4090 (UD-Q4_K_XL); compute-sanitizer memcheck, racecheck and synccheck of the tensor-core kernel (A6000, 32 slots, forced on): no errors.
```

- Связанные решения:
  - `expert-harness`: ours — Сохранить fork CTest/harness; upstream additions объединены без удаления sub8-off проверки.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
The chunk (prompt tokens per forward step, default 512) limited prefill: RTX 5090, strata-inkling --bench, one stream, 4K prompt, SQ-20: 512 -> 8.1K tok/s,
1024 -> 9.5K, 2048 -> 10.5K, 4096 -> 10.7K (16K prompt 7.0K -> 8.9K at 2048, 32K 6.1K -> 7.5K); UD-Q4_K_XL 4.07K -> 4.47K at 2048, flat after; nothing
is lost up to 8192. A bigger chunk costs working memory: the runner and K/V took 1460 / 1822 / 2710 / 4558 MiB at chunk 512 / 1024 / 2048 / 4096 on an
RTX 4090 (SQ-20 all resident, 5255 MiB free after the experts; the engine caps max_batch at 4096) and 1440 / 1804 MiB at 512 / 1024 on an RTX 3060 Ti
8 GB, where 2048 did not fit and the halve-on-fail retry (859276060) brought it back to 1024.

- strata/core/ink_chunk.hpp: ink_auto_chunk(free_after_load_mib, slots): the largest of 2048 / 1024 that fits (the memory the runner takes at that chunk
  + 1500 MiB margin for K/V growth, the drafter and the desktop), else 512; capped by the slot count: 2048 for 1-3 slots, 1024 for 4-15, 512 from 16.
  The experts are placed first, with their reserve computed for chunk 512, so a bigger chunk never displaces an expert: a hybrid card with little left
  keeps 512, a card whose experts are all resident gets 2048. Test ink_chunk_test (the 4090 and 3060 Ti ledgers, the cap, monotone in memory).
- InkCudaBackend::init resolves the chunk after the experts are placed and logs "[InkCUDA] prefill chunk N (auto: M MiB free after the experts, S slot(s);
  --chunk N sets it)"; effective_chunk() reports what the runner really got; ink_serve (token_budget) and --bench use it. --chunk N still wins,
  STRATA_INK_CHUNK_AUTO=0 keeps 512. HIP, SYCL, Metal and CPU keep 512 (BackendOpts::chunk_auto is read only by the CUDA backend).
- The slot cap comes from the mixed-work case, 32 slots, a 16K prompt arriving among 31 decoders, longest wait of a decoding slot at chunk 512 / 1024 /
  2048: RTX 3060 Ti 8 GB (SQ-10 hybrid) 2322 / 2210 / 43,424 ms (the long prompt read in 91 / 56 / 218 s); RTX 4090 (SQ-20 resident) 2096 / 3974 ms with the
  long prompt at 108 / 110 s; RTX 3060 12 GB 3897 ms at 512, 2804 ms at 1024. Throughput of 32 requests of 512 tokens at once (prompt + output tok/s):
  8 GB 55 (512) / 83 (1024) / 125 (2048); 12 GB 65 / 95; 4090 43 / 51. These ran on boxes whose CPUs were loaded by other jobs: relative numbers only.
- Equivalence: RTX 4090 SQ-20 (resident): greedy tokens identical between the auto chunk (2048) and --chunk 512 for prompts of 15, 200, 3000, 16000 and 30000
  tokens; serve prefill 3000 / 16000 / 30000 tokens 2788 / 2979 / 4608 -> 3088 / 3247 / 5053 tok/s. Hybrid SQ-10 (8 and 12 GB): identical up to 3000
  tokens, different at 16K (and 30K on the 8 GB card) between the two chunks, with the 512 runs of the two cards also differing from each other (expert
  promotion of the hybrid path); a same-chunk repeat is queued.
- No OOM and no retry in any gate run (8 / 12 / 24 GB, 1 and 32 slots).
```

### `6e9415252eba` — perf(inkling2/cuda): sm_120 FP4 / MX8 expert kernels ask for 128 contiguous bytes of each weight row ahead of time, the gate/up phase gets 35% faster at 64 slots

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_moe_fp4_sm120.cu` (+49/-16)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
k_moe_sf4_tc and k_moe_mx8_tc read the expert weights 32 bytes of a row per K step, 128 rows 1,152 or 2,304 bytes apart. On an RTX 5090 the gate/up phase of SQ-20 at
64 slots took 20.6 ms for 18.3 GB, 0.92 TB/s, about half of the card's bandwidth, while the down phase (80%) was fine. A cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 of the next 128 bytes of each
row, issued by one thread per row every 4 steps (and the first window plus the block-scale row of gate/up before the first step), takes gate/up to 13.1 ms at 64 slots
and 16.2 -> 10.0 ms at 32 slots; windows of 64 / 128 / 192 / 256 B are within 5% of each other, 512 B and above are worse, a prefetch for the down kernel (576 B rows)
gives nothing and stays off. A prefetch is a hint: no result changes.

Total decode on the 5090 (SQ-20, --bench 128 prompt, fp8 KV, 2 alternating rounds): 64 slots 931 / 928 -> 1,065 / 1,053 tok/s (+13%), 32 slots 648 / 644 -> 774 / 773 (+20%);
8 slots (below the 24 tokens where this kernel is used) equal within noise.

STRATA_INK_SM120_PF (gate/up, default 128) and STRATA_INK_SM120_PFD (down, default 0) set the window in bytes per row, a multiple of 32; 0 turns it off.

Gate: logits of a 400-token sequence fed in chunks of 400 / 64 / 32 / 24 / 8 are bit-identical to the tree without the prefetch for SQ-20 and UD-Q4_K_XL on an RTX 5090
(the build that gave these numbers; the commit is the same kernel file). compute-sanitizer memcheck of the two kernels is queued on the 5090.
```

### `22b32fc879ff` — launch: a --kv the Inkling engine does not take is said, not dropped; test that the allowed ones reach it for a GGUF and a .strata file (GRID, #6681 follow-up)

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `terminal/strata_cli/launch/runner.py` (+5/-0)
  - `terminal/strata_cli/launch/settings.py` (+16/-0)
  - `terminal/tests/terminal/test_launch.py` (+31/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
0.2.20 accepted `--kv k8v4` for an Inkling GGUF started with --model-path and
wrote no --kv into the engine arguments (it had no Inkling kv handling at all),
so the 8-bit comparison ran on the default. rc1 passes the allowed values
(fp16, fp8, k8v8, k8v4 on CUDA; fp16, fp8 on HIP, Metal and SYCL, where k8v4 /
k8v8 become fp8) for both file kinds, since the run config of either is the
same family; a test pins that. What was still dropped quietly was a value
the engine does not take: a Qwen format (int8, q4_0), which the launch
command accepts for every family. The launch now says so, once, in the
notices and as a warning (settings.inkling_kv_note), and also says when
k8v4 / k8v8 become fp8 on a HIP, Metal or SYCL card.
```

### `c77e47d953a4` — inkling2/cuda: STRATA_INK_PROF=2 prints the phases of every prefill chunk

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_cuda_backend.cu` (+2/-1)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_runner.cuh` (+9/-1)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
STRATA_INK_PROF=1 only printed the decode groups. With =2 each prefill chunk of 64 or more
tokens prints one PREFILL-M<n> line (res_ctrl, dense_qkv, sconv_kv, attn, dense_wo, moe and the
moe parts), so a chunk can be split into dense / attention / MoE time. Diagnostic only: it runs
eager with events, nothing changes when the variable is unset.
```

### `fb5973183e88` — inkling2/cuda: STRATA_INK_STEPTIME=1 splits one decode token into host time between steps, call wall time and GPU span

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_cuda_backend.cu` (+42/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
Diagnostic only, off unless the variable is 1. For one-token steps it prints every 100 steps the host time
between two steps (sampling, protocol, batch building), the wall time of the step call (launches, head,
top-K, sync) and the GPU span of the call (first event to the event after the top-K). On an RTX PRO 5000
with SQ-10 the host time between steps is 3-16 microseconds and the call wall time equals the GPU span
(9.04-9.13 ms), so the serving loop leaves the GPU idle about 0.1% of a token.
```

### `0c655e75ecc4` — perf(inkling2/cuda): prefill MoE for sm_80..89 takes 64 tokens of an expert per tile, bit for bit the same results

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_moe_cuda.cuh` (+15/-1)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_moe_prefill.cuh` (+252/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
k_ink_moe_sf4_mx8_fp16tc works on 16 tokens of one expert at a time, so at a 2048-token chunk (about 128
tokens per expert) every FP4 / FP8 weight tile is decoded to FP16 again for each group of 16 tokens and the
expert's activation tile is staged from global memory 8 times per weight block.
k_ink_moe_pf_fp16tc (new file ink_moe_prefill.cuh) takes 64 tokens per tile for chunks of 256 tokens or more
on sm_80..89: the weight tile is decoded once per 64 tokens and the m16n8k16 MMAs run 8 times per decoded
tile. Each output element is accumulated as fma(scale of the 16-block, mma(16 weights, 16 activations), acc) in
the same k order as before and the MMA result of a (row, token) pair does not depend on the other tokens of
the tile, so the logits do not change. STRATA_INK_PF_TILE=0 keeps the 16-token kernel.

RTX 4090, UD-Q4_K_XL, prompt of 4,096 real-text tokens, chunk 2048, alternating A/B of the variable over 2
rounds (a fresh engine each): prefill 2,402.5 / 2,402.5 tok/s with the 16-token kernel, 2,985.7 / 2,984.2
with the 64-token tile (+24.3%, spread 0.1%); the generated tokens have the same hash in every start. The
dumped logits of 2,100 positions are bit-identical between the two settings at chunks 2048, 1024, 512 and 256.
```

### `04e427a589ca` — test(inkling2/cuda): INK_PF_FAULTTEST makes the prefill tile kernel read out of bounds, to prove a filtered memcheck covers it

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_moe_prefill.cuh` (+10/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
Compiled only with -DINK_PF_FAULTTEST (a test build, never a release build): the first block of k_ink_moe_pf_fp16tc
reads one float far outside every allocation. A compute-sanitizer memcheck with --kernel-name regex=k_ink_moe_pf_fp16tc
on the test build must report it; on the release build the same command must be clean.

RTX 4090, UD-Q4_K_XL, bench prompt of 2,100 tokens at chunk 2048: the test build ends with rc 9 and "Invalid __global__
read of size 4 bytes at k_ink_moe_pf_fp16tc<true, 8>" (8 errors); the release build under the same command: 0 errors.
```

### `4655f3b53306` — perf(inkling2/cuda): the L2 prefetch of the MX8 expert kernel on sm_120 is opt-in (STRATA_INK_SM120_PF_MX8), the FP4 kernel keeps it on

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_moe_fp4_sm120.cu` (+17/-6)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
The FP4 kernel (k_moe_sf4_tc) has its compute-sanitizer memcheck; the MX8 kernel (k_moe_mx8_tc, layers 20-23 of a native NVFP4 file such as SQ-20) has only the bit-identity
check, so its prefetch window is now 0 unless STRATA_INK_SM120_PF_MX8 asks for one (1 = 128 B, or a window in bytes, a multiple of 32). With the default the kernel runs
exactly the pre-prefetch code path (the window argument is 0 and every prefetch branch is skipped). The down kernels get no prefetch for either format. The MX8 prefetch
becomes the default after its memcheck has run.
```

### `d371292911d1` — inkling2/metal: logits of every request that ends its prompt in a batch of more than 64 rows

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `engine/src/inkling2/ink_main.cpp` (+2/-2)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/metal/ink_metal_backend.mm` (+8/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/metal/ink_metal_runner.h` (+24/-6)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/metal/test_metal_batch_logits_live.py` (+56/-0)
  - `engine/src/inkling2/test_metal_ckpt_contract.py` (+14/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
The runner unembeds the first min(M, 64) rows of a batch when the batch asks
for the logits of several rows. With --parallel > 1 and prompts that end in the
same scheduler iteration (32 clients sending long documents together), the
wanted rows (each request's last prompt token) lie further down the batch and
came back as zeros: the first token of those replies was token 0 / a wrong
greedy pick, and a sampled one was drawn from nothing. The share of wrong
replies grew with the slot count (0 of 32 at one slot, 3 at 8, 9 at 32 in the
0.2.21 release grid). Alone, slot 0's prompt-end logits had a KL of about 10
against the solo run.

InkBatchStep.logits_rows names the rows; the runner copies them next to each
other and unembeds those. The backend sets it when the batch has more than 64
rows. --batch-check exits 1 above KL 1.0.

Tests: test_metal_ckpt_contract.py (source contract) and
metal/test_metal_batch_logits_live.py (real engine, --batch-check at 2, 4 and 8
slots: step 0 top-1 equal and KL under 1).
```

### `264b155dd75a` — serve: stop starting an engine that keeps dying, and say why (#6896 #6830 #6849)

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `terminal/serve/server.py` (+63/-0)
  - `terminal/serve/test_crash_loop_restart.py` (+125/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
An engine that died at its start or on its first request was started again by
every request that found it dead, with no limit and no message (375 failed
starts in five hours on one machine; the app showed nothing). Three deaths of
one engine within ten minutes now stop the restarts: the request gets a 503
that names the last error line the engine left, its log file and, when the
error is the Q8_0 tensor-core fault of #6713 ("layer 0 never rang" /
"operation not supported on global/shared address space"), the way out
(update to 0.2.21, or STRATA_HC_Q8_TC=0 and STRATA_HC_Q8_BF16TC=0 in the
run config env). One death counts once however many requests find it dead; a
model that was unloaded is not a crash; a request after ten minutes tries
again, as the fatal-GPU limit already did. Every client of the server (the
app's chat, the agent, the Terminal) gets the same message.

Tests: serve/test_crash_loop_restart.py (two restarts then refusal over 50
requests; a start that itself fails; the workaround text and the fault line
found above the last log line; the window; unload).
```

### `6a6e56d55765` — serve: the crash-loop limit leaves a missing engine program alone (fixes serve.test_ready_timeout.SpawnFailure after 264b155dd)

- Дата: 2026-11-23
- Автор: Niko1221
- Файлы:
  - `terminal/serve/server.py` (+3/-4)
  - `terminal/serve/test_crash_loop_restart.py` (+17/-0)

- Связанные решения:
  - Прямого решения в matrix нет; изменение принято как upstream-база.

**Исходное сообщение commit**

```
An engine whose program is missing or cannot be run never has a process, and
every request already answers "the engine could not be started: ..." at once
with its own plain reason. The limit counted those tries too, so the fourth
request got the crash-loop text instead (serve.test_ready_timeout asks four in
a row). A start with no process is no longer counted; only a process that
existed and died is. Test added in test_crash_loop_restart.py.
```
